source.author: verg
source.text: Ille etiam exstincto miseratus Caesare Romam, cum caput obscura nitidum ferrugine texit inpiaque aeternam timuerunt saecula noctem.
source.text_original: Ille etiam exstincto miseratus Caesare Romam, / cum caput obscura nitidum ferrugine texit / inpiaque aeternam timuerunt saecula noctem.
source.text_english: He too, pitying Rome when Caesar was extinguished, covered his shining head with murky gloom, and the impious ages feared an everlasting night.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Inclytus autem erat, et decorus aspectu, quando ad passionem ejus terra contremuit, saxa dirupta sunt, et fugiente sole, aeternam noctem elementa timuerunt.
reuse.text_original: Inclytus autem erat, et decorus aspectu, quando ad passionem ejus terra contremuit, saxa dirupta sunt, et fugiente sole, aeternam noctem elementa timuerunt.
reuse.text_english: But he was illustrious and comely in appearance, when, at his Passion, the earth trembled, rocks were split apart, and the sun fled, and the elements feared an eternal night.
